claims.text: A route deviation is established on this trip's own telemetry. The GPS trace measures 34.17 km against a booked optimal of 27.1 km, an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests therefore pass: the excess exceeds 20% of optimal and exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms. The trace figure governs; the rounded 34.2 km copy on the trip record is expressly not citable for the threshold test.

The trace needs no corroboration, because it is not impaired for policy purposes. POL-RD-07 impairs a trace only on a gap above 90 seconds, a straight-line jump above 500 m, or a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. This trace runs 283 fixes at a 10-second interval with 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0 and an empty gaps list, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires; the deviation stands on the trace alone and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged and has shifted to the driver. All three artifacts describe the same trip: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown each carry TRP-00104, and the trace's first fix at 20:35:10 matches trip_record.started_at at 20:35:10. The excess above the POL-RD-01 threshold is measured from an unimpaired trace. The additional-corroboration proviso does not apply, because rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1, nowhere near the four-claims/one-substantiated configuration the clause names. It is now for the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause.

The driver's second advisory carries nothing, and I disclose that I am relying on an impaired artifact to say so. EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is IMPAIRED at weight 0.25 with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE: its geometry is the CTE after Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, a corridor the trace never enters at any point, so intersects_route is false, and it was entered through the operator console rather than ingested from the LTA feed. POL-RD-03 exonerates only where the advisory names a road the optimal route traverses; this one names a corridor this trip never uses, so it cannot support any exoneration.

Taken at its highest, the driver's PIE advisory exonerates only part of the excess, and the rest is refundable to the rider. POL-RD-03 caps the justified excess at the lesser of the measured excess and 1.30 x (shortest lawful alternative minus booked optimal) plus 1.00 km. On this record that is min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km. The 2.17 km of excess beyond that cap is not exonerated, and the driver's 34.17 km is 4.07 km longer than even the 30.1 km shortest lawful alternative.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. Against the closure-adjusted optimal route of 27.1 + 4.90 = 32.00 km, with duration scaled to 40.1 minutes, recomputed_fare = 3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1 + 0.80 platform fee = 39.828. Charged total 43.41; recomputed fare 39.828; refund 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded UP to SGD 3.60. The rider is left carrying only the closure-justified part of the trip, not the driver's overrun.

No rider-requested detour reduces that refund. The only rider message is 'ok but not too long ah' (MSG-00104-002); it names no place and no road, and waypoint_hint is null on both messages. The route was proposed by the driver, not requested by the rider. On the clause's own terms the corroboration test is undecidable and POL-RD-04 is unavailable, so no excess is excluded on this ground. To whatever extent the rider's 'ok' was consent, it was expressly conditioned on the detour not being long, a condition a 34.17 km drive against a 30.1 km shortest lawful alternative did not meet.

There is no relocation to re-baseline against. Both pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null on the trip record, as are original_pickup and original_dropoff, so POL-RD-05 does not run and the baseline stays the booked 27.1 km optimal.

There is no repeat-pattern uplift, and no pattern finding either way. POL-RD-06 is engaged only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation; this one is not material, because 7.07 km of excess and 26.09% are each below the 8.0 km and 50% tests, and only 2.17 km of excess remains after the POL-RD-03 adjustment. In any event the pattern test fails on the field the clause names: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 288, a rate of 0.0035, far below the 0.05 threshold. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not the field POL-RD-06 asks for and cannot be substituted for it.

On pass-throughs the rider's honest position is that nothing extra is due. erp_lines is empty on this trip and tolls_erp is 0.00; the trip neither originates at nor ends at an airport, so no surcharge correction arises. The POL-RD-02 refund already comprehends third-party pass-throughs and must not be topped up, so the SGD 3.60 figure is not understated on that account.

If the panel finds POL-RD-03(c) unmet, no part of the excess is exonerated and the reverse arithmetic runs on the booked optimal: recomputed_fare = 3.80 + 0.75 x 27.1 + 0.28 x 34.0 + 0.80 = 34.445, so refund = 43.41 - 34.445 = 8.965, rounded UP to SGD 9.00. The record supports that reading: limb (c) requires the actual route to leave the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoin it after, but trip_record.optimal_route_source records the optimal as PIE westbound throughout, while the trace summary records the rejoin as occurring on the AYE, not on the PIE.

claims.text: The trace measures 34.17 km against a 27.1 km booked optimal, an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09%. That passes POL-RD-01's establishment test (over 20% and over 0.8 km), but it fails BOTH materiality thresholds: 7.07 km is below the 8.0 km absolute figure and 26.09% is far below the 50% relative figure. This is therefore an established but NON-MATERIAL deviation, so POL-RD-06's pattern check is not engaged. Even if it were, the driver profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 1 (below the 3 required) and 1 flag across 288 completed_trips_90d, a ratio of 0.003 against the 0.05 required. No pattern and no conduct referral arises.

The optimal route is PIE westbound throughout. LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260716-007 describes a multi-vehicle accident on the 'Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Tuas, after Eunos Link exit', two of three lanes blocked, severity HIGH. It therefore names the very road and segment the optimal route traverses - limb (a) of POL-RD-03 - and the artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The advisory ran 20:02 to 21:35 and the trip ran 20:35:10 to 21:22:10, an overlap of 53.1 minutes. A PIE westbound trip from Tampines reaches the post-Eunos segment early in its run, inside that window even before the 15-minute buffer at each end is applied. Limb (b) of POL-RD-03 is satisfied.

The trace shows the vehicle leaving the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 ahead of the blocked segment and rejoining on the AYE afterwards - out of the optimal corridor before the affected stretch and back into it after, which is limb (c) of POL-RD-03. The trace is COMPLETE: 100% coverage, 283 fixes at a 10-second interval, no gaps and max_gap_sec of 0.0, so nothing in POL-RD-07 is engaged.

Exoneration is capped and the cap is arithmetic. The justified excess is min(7.07 km, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km. The closure-adjusted optimal distance is 27.1 + 4.90 = 32.00 km and the adjusted duration is 34.0 x (32.00/27.1) = 40.1 minutes. The excess up to 4.90 km is the driver's excused response to a HIGH-severity accident, not a deviation he must answer for.

POL-RD-02 therefore runs against the closure-adjusted optimal, not the booked one: recomputed fare = 3.80 base + (0.75 x 32.00) + (0.28 x 40.1) + 0.80 platform fee, at surge 1.0 with no ERP = 39.828. Refund = 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60. That $3.60 is the whole of the rider's monetary remedy on this trip; the asserted $14 overcharge is roughly four times what the policy arithmetic supports.

The rider carries the initial burden and has met it, but the burden then shifts to the driver, and the driver discharges it with a specific artifact and a specific clause - LTA advisory ADV-20260716-007 under POL-RD-03 - not with a bare assertion that traffic was bad. POL-RD-08 is satisfied on the driver's side.

The chat log records the driver telling the rider at 20:38:12 'accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok' and the rider replying at 20:38:55 'ok but not too long ah'. The diversion was disclosed before it was driven and the rider assented to it; the trace leaves the PIE before the blocked segment and rejoins on the AYE, consistent with the route named in the message. This was not a unilateral detour. On the reading that the rider's assent is an instruction to take the ECP, the excess between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor is excluded under POL-RD-04. waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so the driver asserts no waypoint corroboration and puts its primary case on POL-RD-03.

There is nothing left to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. The fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines at all (tolls_erp 0.00, erp_gantries empty) and no airport surcharge, so the pass-through correction under POL-RD-09 yields nothing further to refund - and equally nothing to bolt on as a separate line.

The driver does not rely on the operator-entered CTE breakdown advisory. EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is impaired, weight 0.25, with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE; its geometry never intersects the trace and it describes a corridor this trip never entered. The exoneration rests entirely on the COMPLETE LTA advisory ADV-20260716-007, so no finding here depends on the impaired artifact.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — the rider was overcharged, but by less than claimed; the driver's diversion is mostly, not fully, excused.

THE DEVIATION. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00104, weight 1.0) measures 34.17 km against the booked optimal of 27.1 km — an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09%. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so a deviation is established. It is NOT material: 7.07 km is below the 8.0 km absolute test and 26.09% is below the 50% relative test. POL-RD-06 is therefore not engaged, so there is no repeat-pattern uplift and no driver-conduct referral. In any event the pattern test fails on the fields the clause names — driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 288 (rate 0.003, far below 0.05). The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context-only under POL-GEN-01 and is not the field POL-RD-06 asks for; it was correctly not used as a ground.

WHAT IS EXCUSED. LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01, COMPLETE, weight 1.0) names the Pan Island Expressway towards Tuas after the Eunos Link exit — the very road and segment the optimal route uses — and its 20:02–21:35 window overlaps the trip (53.1 min). The trace shows the vehicle leaving the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 before the blocked stretch and rejoining the westbound corridor after it. POL-RD-03 is satisfied. The excused excess is capped: min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km. The driver's 34.17 km is 4.07 km longer than even the shortest lawful alternative (30.1 km), and that overrun beyond the cap is his to answer for. The second, operator-entered CTE advisory (EV-ADVIS-00104-02, weight 0.25, issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE) describes a corridor this trip never enters and carries nothing; the finding does not rest on it and is unaffected by its discount.

THE REFUND. POL-RD-02 runs against the closure-adjusted optimal: distance 27.1 + 4.90 = 32.00 km; duration 34.0 x (32.00/27.1) = 40.1 min. recomputed_fare = 3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1 + 0.80 platform fee = 39.828. charged_total = 43.41. refund = 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded UP to SGD 3.60. That is not de minimis (above SGD 0.50) and well short of the 90% full-refund share, so it is a partial refund.

CLAIMS ANSWERED. The rider's fallback — that limb (c) of POL-RD-03 fails because the trace rejoins on the AYE and not the PIE — is rejected: the evidence records the vehicle leaving the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoining it after, which is what limb (c) requires, and nothing shows the vehicle simply drove an unrelated trip. On the rider's reading the refund would be 43.41 - 34.445 = 8.965, i.e. SGD 9.00 against the booked optimal; that reading is not adopted. The chat log (driver announcing the diversion, rider replying 'ok but not too long ah') is not a rider-requested detour: no waypoint_hint and no road named, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run, the clause is unavailable, and the case is decided on the remaining clauses — no excess is excluded on that ground. No pickup or dropoff amendment exists on the trip record, so POL-RD-05 does not run and the baseline stays the booked 27.1 km. There are no ERP or toll lines and no airport surcharge, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing on top of the POL-RD-02 figure.

NO ESCALATION. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes (100% coverage, 283 fixes at 10 s, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0), so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; identifiers (TRP-00104) and timestamps match; no charge line lacks a counterpart; and the refund is far below the ceiling. No clause produces a referral.

To both parties: the outcome is a partial refund of $3.60.

The distance is not in dispute. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00104, weight 1.0) measures 34.17 km against the booked optimal of 27.1 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00104, weight 1.0) — an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09%. Under POL-RD-01 that is a deviation ESTABLISHED (over 20% and over 0.8 km) but NOT material (under 50% and under 8.0 km). No material-deviation conduct check is engaged, and the driver's 90-day record (1 flag across 288 completed trips, 0.35%) does not meet POL-RD-06's pattern test in any event — so no driver-conduct referral is made. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags was correctly not used for that test and plays no part here.

The diversion is partly excused. The LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01, weight 1.0, COMPLETE) names the PIE towards Tuas after Eunos Link — the road the optimal route uses; its window 20:02–21:35 overlaps the trip; and the trace shows the vehicle leaving the corridor at Bedok North Ave 4 ahead of the blocked stretch and rejoining on the AYE afterwards. That is POL-RD-03 exoneration, capped at the lesser of the measured excess and 1.30 × (30.1 − 27.1) + 1.00 = 4.90 km. So 4.90 km of the 7.07 km is excused; the closure-adjusted optimal is 27.1 + 4.90 = 32.00 km, duration scaled to 40.1 minutes.

There is no relocation to re-baseline against. Both pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null on the trip record, as are original_pickup and original_dropoff, so POL-RD-05 does not run and the baseline stays the booked 27.1 km optimal.

There is no repeat-pattern uplift, and no pattern finding either way. POL-RD-06 is engaged only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation; this one is not material, because 7.07 km of excess and 26.09% are each below the 8.0 km and 50% tests, and only 2.17 km of excess remains after the POL-RD-03 adjustment. In any event the pattern test fails on the field the clause names: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 288, a rate of 0.0035, far below the 0.05 threshold. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not the field POL-RD-06 asks for and cannot be substituted for it.
flags: context-only profile field mentioned in claim text: prior_deviation_flags

ledger.claim: On pass-throughs the rider's honest position is that nothing extra is due. erp_lines is empty on this trip and tolls_erp is 0.00; the trip neither originates at nor ends at an airport, so no surcharge correction arises. The POL-RD-02 refund already comprehends third-party pass-throughs and must not be topped up, so the SGD 3.60 figure is not understated on that account.

If the panel finds POL-RD-03(c) unmet, no part of the excess is exonerated and the reverse arithmetic runs on the booked optimal: recomputed_fare = 3.80 + 0.75 x 27.1 + 0.28 x 34.0 + 0.80 = 34.445, so refund = 43.41 - 34.445 = 8.965, rounded UP to SGD 9.00. The record supports that reading: limb (c) requires the actual route to leave the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoin it after, but trip_record.optimal_route_source records the optimal as PIE westbound throughout, while the trace summary records the rejoin as occurring on the AYE, not on the PIE.

The trace measures 34.17 km against a 27.1 km booked optimal, an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09%. That passes POL-RD-01's establishment test (over 20% and over 0.8 km), but it fails BOTH materiality thresholds: 7.07 km is below the 8.0 km absolute figure and 26.09% is far below the 50% relative figure. This is therefore an established but NON-MATERIAL deviation, so POL-RD-06's pattern check is not engaged. Even if it were, the driver profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 1 (below the 3 required) and 1 flag across 288 completed_trips_90d, a ratio of 0.003 against the 0.05 required. No pattern and no conduct referral arises.

The optimal route is PIE westbound throughout. LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260716-007 describes a multi-vehicle accident on the 'Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Tuas, after Eunos Link exit', two of three lanes blocked, severity HIGH. It therefore names the very road and segment the optimal route traverses - limb (a) of POL-RD-03 - and the artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The advisory ran 20:02 to 21:35 and the trip ran 20:35:10 to 21:22:10, an overlap of 53.1 minutes. A PIE westbound trip from Tampines reaches the post-Eunos segment early in its run, inside that window even before the 15-minute buffer at each end is applied. Limb (b) of POL-RD-03 is satisfied.

The trace shows the vehicle leaving the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 ahead of the blocked segment and rejoining on the AYE afterwards - out of the optimal corridor before the affected stretch and back into it after, which is limb (c) of POL-RD-03. The trace is COMPLETE: 100% coverage, 283 fixes at a 10-second interval, no gaps and max_gap_sec of 0.0, so nothing in POL-RD-07 is engaged.

Exoneration is capped and the cap is arithmetic. The justified excess is min(7.07 km, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km. The closure-adjusted optimal distance is 27.1 + 4.90 = 32.00 km and the adjusted duration is 34.0 x (32.00/27.1) = 40.1 minutes. The excess up to 4.90 km is the driver's excused response to a HIGH-severity accident, not a deviation he must answer for.

POL-RD-02 therefore runs against the closure-adjusted optimal, not the booked one: recomputed fare = 3.80 base + (0.75 x 32.00) + (0.28 x 40.1) + 0.80 platform fee, at surge 1.0 with no ERP = 39.828. Refund = 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60. That $3.60 is the whole of the rider's monetary remedy on this trip; the asserted $14 overcharge is roughly four times what the policy arithmetic supports.

The rider carries the initial burden and has met it, but the burden then shifts to the driver, and the driver discharges it with a specific artifact and a specific clause - LTA advisory ADV-20260716-007 under POL-RD-03 - not with a bare assertion that traffic was bad. POL-RD-08 is satisfied on the driver's side.

The chat log records the driver telling the rider at 20:38:12 'accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok' and the rider replying at 20:38:55 'ok but not too long ah'. The diversion was disclosed before it was driven and the rider assented to it; the trace leaves the PIE before the blocked segment and rejoins on the AYE, consistent with the route named in the message. This was not a unilateral detour. On the reading that the rider's assent is an instruction to take the ECP, the excess between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor is excluded under POL-RD-04. waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so the driver asserts no waypoint corroboration and puts its primary case on POL-RD-03.

There is nothing left to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. The fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines at all (tolls_erp 0.00, erp_gantries empty) and no airport surcharge, so the pass-through correction under POL-RD-09 yields nothing further to refund - and equally nothing to bolt on as a separate line.

The driver does not rely on the operator-entered CTE breakdown advisory. EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is impaired, weight 0.25, with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE; its geometry never intersects the trace and it describes a corridor this trip never entered. The exoneration rests entirely on the COMPLETE LTA advisory ADV-20260716-007, so no finding here depends on the impaired artifact.
